references.text: The basic instruction regarding the burnt offering that Leviticus 6:2 refers to as 'torat ha'olah' (the law of the burnt offering)
The daily burnt offering that was to be offered morning and evening, connected with the fire that was to burn all night
The regulations concerning the continual burnt offering, one lamb in the morning and one in the evening
The continuation of the instruction that the fire on the altar must never go out
Aaron and his sons were to tend the lamps, parallel to their responsibility for the altar
Abraham's offering of Isaac as a burnt offering, the earliest detailed description of a burnt offering in the Torah
The book of Hebrews explains how the Levitical burnt offerings were shadows of Christ's perfect sacrifice
Paul urges believers to present themselves as living sacrifices, a spiritual parallel to the burnt offering
